entrypoints.summary: The interactive menu exposes the complete crewmate list, prints the per-round salt, emits a base64 task token on request, and accepts an impostor-name report.
The container runs the Python challenge under socat on a TCP listener at port 12001.

affected_components.role: Discloses candidates and salt, derives the impostor key, emits the token, and accepts the final identity report.
Defines the deterministic tag generation and verification algorithm used by issued task tokens.

sources.concept: public finite candidate identities and round salt

impact.affected_asset: Secrecy of the selected impostor identity and, after the prescribed successful-round sequence, the service flag output.
impact.attacker_capability: Derive and test each public candidate identity's key locally, submit the matching name, and potentially advance through the challenge rounds.
impact.security_effect: Disclosure of the round's hidden impostor identity through offline matching against an issued authentication tag.

causal_trace.summary: Each round selects the hidden impostor from a list of 512 generated crewmate names; the service discloses that complete list and the 12-byte round salt to the participant.

The master key is deterministically derived by HKDF from the selected impostor name and the disclosed salt. Consequently, every disclosed candidate name and salt yields a locally derivable candidate master key.

Generate task returns ciphertext concatenated with an authentication tag computed from the impostor-derived key, public associated data, the disclosed salt used as nonce, and the ciphertext. The AEMC implementation shows how its MAC key and tag are computed, providing a comparison predicate for candidate-derived keys.

A participant can infer the intended offline procedure: recompute a tag for the observed ciphertext under each public-name candidate key and identify the candidate whose tag matches, then submit that name to the report operation. A correct report advances a round; 20 successful rounds reach the flag-print branch.

failure.operation: Emission of an AEMC ciphertext-and-tag token under an impostor-derived key

primary_invariant.kind: secret-key entropy independent of enumerable identity
primary_invariant.statement: An issued authenticated token must not be verifiable under a key that is deterministically derivable from a publicly enumerable identity and publicly disclosed salt.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The hidden identity is selected from a disclosed finite list, while HKDF derives the token key solely from that identity, the disclosed salt, and fixed public context; the issued token exposes a tag that the implementation permits recomputing for each candidate key.

quality.review_notes: Primary challenge source and crypto helper source support the inferred key-enumeration and tag-comparison mechanism. The bundle contains a runnable TCP configuration, but no solver, captured interaction, or execution result demonstrates the proposed matching procedure or completion of all rounds. No shipped remediation patch is supplied; mitigation is code-derived.

remediation.invariant_restored: Keys used to authenticate participant-visible tokens retain secret entropy not reconstructible from the candidate list and the disclosed round salt, so a token tag cannot distinguish the selected identity by offline candidate testing.
mitigation_classes: introduce server-secret key entropy independent of public candidate identities
avoid exposing an authentication-tag verifier under an identity-derived key

state_context.attacker_state_setup: Obtain the printed player list and round salt, request a task token, then derive candidate keys and compare candidate tags before reporting a name.
data_structure_invariants: The impostor is one element of the generated crewmate list.
The displayed salt has the 12-byte length required by AEMC.
The token is ciphertext followed by a 16-byte authentication tag.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The challenge fixes the list size at 512 names per round.
numeric_domains.name: candidate-player-count

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The service prints the randomly generated salt for the active round.
numeric_domains.name: round-salt

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The tag is appended to the issued ciphertext and can be compared locally after recomputation.
numeric_domains.name: authentication-tag

state_context.state_machine: For each round, the service initializes 512 crewmates, chooses one impostor, presents menu actions, and ends the round when a report is submitted. Correct reports increment the global round; the flag branch is reached after the configured maximum rounds.

target.component: interactive impostor-identification service and AEMC token construction
